# Bytecode Example

This document demonstrates how CVM++ source code is compiled into bytecode instructions.

## Source Code

```c
x = 10;

if(x >= 5){
    print(100);
}
else{
    print(200);
}
```

## Generated Bytecode

```text
0  PUSH 10
1  STORE x

2  LOAD x
3  PUSH 5
4  GTE

5  JMP_IF_FALSE 9

6  PUSH 100
7  PRINT

8  JMP 11

9  PUSH 200
10 PRINT
```

## Instruction Reference

### Stack Operations

```text
PUSH value
LOAD variable
STORE variable
```

### Arithmetic

```text
ADD
SUB
MUL
DIV
```

### Comparisons

```text
GT
LT
GTE
LTE
EQ
NEQ
```

### Control Flow

```text
JMP
JMP_IF_FALSE
```

### Output

```text
PRINT
```

## Execution Flow

The VM executes bytecode sequentially using an instruction pointer.

For conditional statements:

```text
Condition
    ↓
JMP_IF_FALSE
    ↓
Then Block
    ↓
JMP
    ↓
Else Block
```

This design allows CVM++ to execute high-level language constructs using a compact stack-based instruction set.
